theory.intro: To draw a **distance–time graph**, plot the initial time–distance point and the point reached at the end of each stage. The initial point need not be the origin. For the booklet's steady-speed travel stages, join consecutive points with straight lines; stops give horizontal lines. Time goes across, distance goes up. Read the vertical axis label: it may show distance from the start or total distance travelled.
facts: Time is always on the **horizontal** axis and distance on the **vertical** axis.

Plot the elapsed time (or clock time) and the distance reading at the end of each stage. Distance from the start decreases on a return journey; total distance travelled never decreases and stays constant during stops.
A stationary stage is drawn **horizontal** — time passes but the distance reading does not change.
On a graph of distance from the start, a return stage slopes down; the line touches the time axis when the traveller reaches the location from which distance is measured.
Check the scale on both axes before plotting: one grid line rarely stands for one unit.
If a stage gives a speed and a time rather than a distance, work the distance out with $d=st$ first.
steps: Work out the initial time and distance reading and the reading at the end of each stage, using what the vertical axis measures.
Plot the initial point and each stage endpoint on the grid.
For the booklet's steady-speed stage model, join consecutive points with straight line segments; draw stops as horizontal segments.

workedExamples.question_text: A walker travels $9$ km from the start in $3$ hours at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph.
A cyclist rides $10$ km from the start in $40$ minutes, rests for $20$ minutes, then rides a further $14$ km in $40$ minutes. Each riding stage is at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph.

A runner travels $6$ km from home in $25$ minutes, rests for $10$ minutes, then returns home in $35$ minutes. Both running stages are at steady speeds. Draw a graph of distance from home against time.

A motorist travels $18$ km away from the start in $0.5$ hours, stops for $0.75$ hours, then travels a further $24$ km away in $1.25$ hours. Both driving stages are at steady speeds. Draw the distance–time graph.

A motorist leaves home at 11:10 am and travels $12$ km by 11:40 am. She stops for $20$ minutes, then travels a further $18$ km by 12:30 pm. She returns home in $60$ minutes. Each driving stage is at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph using minutes after 11:10 am.

Aria cycles $24$ km away from home in $2$ hours, stops for $30$ minutes, then cycles straight home in $1$ hour. Both cycling stages are at steady speeds. Draw a graph of distance from home against elapsed time in hours.
A delivery vehicle starts $600$ m from its depot and travels straight back at a steady speed, arriving $3$ minutes later. Draw a graph of distance from the depot against elapsed time.

A car drives $60$ km away from home in $1$ hour, then stops for $30$ minutes. It next drives straight home at a steady $30$ km/h. Draw the complete graph of distance from home against elapsed time in hours.

A motorist leaves home and drives away at $60$ km/h for $20$ minutes, stops for $15$ minutes, then continues away at $40$ km/h for $1$ hour $15$ minutes. Draw a graph of distance from home against elapsed time in minutes.

Noah leaves home at 7:20 am and walks $2$ km to a station, arriving at 7:40 am. His train leaves immediately and travels a further $12$ km in $20$ minutes. He waits $10$ minutes for a bus, which travels a further $6$ km and reaches school at 8:40 am. All travel is away from home along the same route; use steady speeds for the travel stages. Draw a distance–time graph using clock time.

foundation.question_text: A driver leaves home, travels $40$ km in $1$ hour, stops for $1$ hour, then drives straight home in $2$ hours. Both driving stages are at steady speeds. Draw a graph of distance from home against elapsed time in hours.

development.question_text: A motorist leaves home at $9{:}15$ am and reaches a beach $36$ km away at $10{:}00$ am. She stays for $1$ hour $15$ minutes, then drives straight home, arriving at $12{:}45$ pm. Both driving stages are at steady speeds. Draw a graph of distance from home against minutes after $9{:}15$ am.

mastery.question_text: Mia leaves home at $7{:}05$ am and walks $1.5$ km to a station, arriving at $7{:}25$ am. Her train leaves immediately and travels a further $18$ km in $25$ minutes. She waits $15$ minutes for a bus, which travels a further $6.5$ km and reaches school at $8{:}40$ am. All travel is away from home along the same route; use steady speeds for the travel stages. Draw a graph of distance from home against minutes after $7{:}05$ am.
